Dinesh vs Prateek on 5 December, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:35703
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 5 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 2966 of 2025
 Dinesh
 Versus
 Prateek And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Himanshu Paliwal, learned counsel for the appellan
 Shri Bhaskar Agrawal, Advocate with Shri Pradip Kumar G
 counsel for respondent No.2 / Insurance Company.
 Order

The appellant has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 17.12.2024 passed by the learned 9t h Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.1881/2023, whereby challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The liability of the Insurance Company is not in dispute, hence, the matter is being heard in absence of the owner and driver of the vehicle.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 10.07.2022 at around 12:30 PM, the appellant was returning after delivering an order placed through Zomato Online application.

When he reached near Jakir Hotel, Scheme No.94, Indore, respondent No.1, who was driving his Ford car bearing registration number MP- 19-CC-515 in a rash and negligent manner, rammed into the appellant's motorcycle, as a result of which the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
The incident was reported at Police Station Lasudiya, Indore.

3.1 The appellant suffered grievous injuries on various parts of his body NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35703 2 MA-2966-2025 including both upper and lower limbs.
He was taken to M.Y. Hospital and thereafter to Bhandari Hospital for treatment.
He suffered several fractures and incised woulds on his left leg, which resulted in permanent disability.
The appellant was 38 years of age at the time of the accident and claimed that he was earning Rs.24,000/- per month.
3.2 He filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the aforesaid accident.

The Tribunal after recording evidence held Dinesh vs Prateek on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65022064/
1 that the accident occurred due to the fault of the insured vehicle and awarded total compensation of Rs.60,779/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, while concluding in para 16 that the appellant had sustained 10% permanent disability with respect to the whole body, the tribunal surprisingly held such disability had not resulted in any loss of earning capacity on the ground that the doctor had certified only physical disability and had not assessed functional loss of earning capacity.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the job assigned to the Claims Tribunal has wrongly been held to be performed by the doctor.

He submits that the doctor has correctly issued the certificate of permanent physical disability, which ought to have been considered by the Claims Tribunal for assessing the loss of earning capacity.
However, the Tribunal failed to do so and awarded only a meagre sum of Rs. 60,779/- for the injuries sustained by the appellant.

He further submits that even under other heads, the Tribunal has awarded only a nominal amount of compensation."
5 .
Per contra , learned counsel for the Insurance Company supports the findings of the award and submits that the appellant was working as a labourer and is capable of continuing with his job.
Therefore, the Claims Tribunal rightly did NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35703 3 MA-2966-2025 not award any amount towards loss of earning capacity.

He further submits that on applying the functional disability test laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 , the finding of the Claims Tribunal are correct.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
7.
On perusal of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in para 16, it is clear that the Tribunal accepted the permanent disability certificate (Ex. P-34).
However, despite doing so, it proceeded in para 25 to hold that the doctor had not certified any loss of earning capacity.
Consequently, no compensation was awarded towards the permanent disability sustained by the appellant.
8. In the considered view of this Court, the approach adopted by the Claims Tribunal is patently incorrect.

As laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case o f Raj Kumar (Supra) , it was the duty of the Claims Tribunal to assess the resultant loss of earning capacity by applying the functional disability test as propounded by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the said decision.

9. Considering the facts of the present case and the undisputed position that the appellant was working as a delivery boy for the Zomato Online application, the Tribunal ought to have taken into account the loss of earning capacity in relation to the injuries sustained by the appellant.
10. In the considered view of this Court, considering that the appellant was a delivery boy, he must have operated a two-wheeler to deliver goods as per orders.
11. Accordingly, the extent of permanent disability with respect to loss of earning capacity also is taken at 10%, as certified by the doctor.
However, considering that even under other heads, only a meagre amount of compensation has been awarded.

Dinesh vs Prateek on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65022064/
2
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35703 4 MA-2966-2025 12.

This Court is of the considered view that instead of quantifying of compensation under different heads, a lump sum amount of Rs.2,50,000/- would constitute a just and fair compensation in the present case.

13. It is therefore directed that the appellant be paid a total amount of Rs.2,50,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal which shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal.
14. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Dinesh vs Prateek on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65022064/
